findings.highlight: Please don't put it that way…
findings.explanation: Haruki says that hearing Hamada put it that way is a relief or something he appreciates. The English makes him ask Hamada not to say it, reversing his response to being released from guilt over resigning.

findings.highlight: I doubt I'll choose this path again.
findings.evidenceJa:
それは多分、
もう選ばれるはずのない進路だったけど。
findings.explanation: Kaiousha is a career path that is probably no longer available to Haruki; the English says he doubts he will choose it again.
findings.japanese:
それは多分、
もう選ばれるはずのない進路だったけど。
findings.todokanai: I doubt I'll choose this path again.

findings.highlight: it's amplifying the tortuous, anxious feeling that's festering within me
findings.evidenceJa: その痛みの思った以上の激しさは、自分の中にわだかまる、焦りにも似た感情によって増幅されているせいかもしれない。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks his festering anxiety may be amplifying the physical pain of the cold wind. The English says the pain is amplifying the anxiety, reversing cause and effect in the body/feeling comparison.
findings.japanese:
その痛みの思った以上の激しさは、
自分の中にわだかまる、焦りにも似た感情によって
増幅されているせいかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: The pain feels more extreme than I expected it to be, perhaps because it's amplifying the tortuous, anxious feeling that's festering within me.

findings.highlight: I never asked anyone to do it with me.
findings.evidenceJa: 『本当は昔から一度はやってみたかったんだ。ただ、わたしってインドア派のイメージあったし、実際そうだったから今まで声かからなかったんだよね』
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that because everyone correctly saw her as indoorsy, nobody had ever invited her. The English says she never invited anyone herself, reversing the social agency and losing why Io's invitation matters to her.
findings.japanese:
『本当は昔から一度はやってみたかったんだ。
ただ、わたしってインドア派のイメージあったし、
実際そうだったから今まで声かからなかったんだよね』
findings.todokanai: "The truth is, I've been meaning to try something like this for a long time. It's just that everyone's had the perception of me being an indoorsy person, and it wasn't exactly wrong either, so I never asked anyone to do it with me."

findings.highlight: The moment I heard you weren't going, I found myself at a loss.
findings.evidenceJa: 『…春希くんが行かないって言ったとき、どうしようか、迷ってる』
findings.explanation: Setsuna is wondering what she will do if Haruki says he is not going. The English says she has already heard that he will not go, contradicting Haruki's later reply that he has not decided and erasing her indirect attempt to learn his choice.
findings.japanese:
『…春希くんが行かないって言ったとき、
どうしようか、迷ってる』
findings.todokanai: "…The moment I heard you weren't going, I found myself at a loss."

findings.highlight: Setsuna also knowing that she's wavering because my feelings are no longer directed at her
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は、俺の気持ちが自分じゃない方に揺れたのを感じ取っているのに。
findings.explanation: Setsuna has sensed that Haruki's feelings wavered toward someone other than her. The English makes Setsuna herself the one wavering, reversing the subject of the emotional movement she has detected.
findings.japanese:
雪菜は、俺の気持ちが自分じゃない方に揺れたのを
感じ取っているのに。
findings.todokanai: And this is despite Setsuna also knowing that she's wavering because my feelings are no longer directed at her.

findings.highlight: the event coordinator shot that idea down pretty quickly
findings.evidenceJa: 『俺も、スキーもスノボもやったことない。研究室でスキー合宿って話が出たけど、幹事権限で潰したくらいだし』
findings.explanation: Haruki says he used his own authority as organizer to kill his seminar's ski-camp proposal, proof of how little he wanted to ski. The English invents a separate event coordinator who killed it, removing Haruki's joke and agency.
findings.japanese:
『俺も、スキーもスノボもやったことない。
研究室でスキー合宿って話が出たけど、
幹事権限で潰したくらいだし』
findings.todokanai: "I've never gone skiing or snowboarding before either. Someone did throw around the idea for a group overnight skiing trip in one of my seminars, but the event coordinator shot that idea down pretty quickly."

findings.highlight: Whoever survives can worry about what to do next.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ま、今日はそんな古いことは忘れて、とりあえず潰れるまで飲みましょう？生き残った方が既成事実を作る方向で」
findings.explanation: Sawako jokes that they should drink until one collapses and the survivor can create a 既成事実—a sexual or romantic fait accompli. The English replaces the punch line with the survivor generically worrying about what to do next.
findings.japanese:
「ま、今日はそんな古いことは忘れて、
とりあえず潰れるまで飲みましょう？
生き残った方が既成事実を作る方向で」
findings.todokanai: "Well, how about we just let bygones be bygones today, and drink until we drop? Whoever survives can worry about what to do next."

findings.highlight: I don't think that simply hitting you a couple times will be nearly enough of a retribution
findings.evidenceJa: 「二、三発殴っても罰あたらないんじゃないかって、そのくらいは思ってるのよ？」
findings.explanation: Sawako says she thinks divine punishment would not strike her even if she hit Haruki two or three times—she would be justified in doing that much. The English says a couple of hits would not be enough punishment, escalating the number and changing her calibrated anger into a demand for more violence.
findings.japanese:
「二、三発殴っても罰あたらないんじゃないかって、
そのくらいは思ってるのよ？」
findings.todokanai: "And do you know that I don't think that simply hitting you a couple times will be nearly enough of a retribution?"

findings.highlight: there's still hope for you if you're ready to face the consequences
findings.evidenceJa: 「わたしが殴っても、麻理の傷は癒えないのよ？…あなたは罰を受けた気になって、少しは救われるのかもしれないけど」
findings.explanation: Sawako refuses because hitting Haruki would not heal Mari; it would only let him feel punished and therefore a little absolved. The English turns this critique of self-serving penance into hopeful approval that he is ready to face consequences.
findings.japanese:
「わたしが殴っても、麻理の傷は癒えないのよ？
…あなたは罰を受けた気になって、
少しは救われるのかもしれないけど」
findings.todokanai: "You know Mari's wounds won't heal even if I do hit you, right? …Though I suppose there's still hope for you if you're ready to face the consequences."

findings.highlight: It's just impossible to persuade her.
findings.evidenceJa: 「特にあいつは、今の段階で圧倒的に不利だからね。…ちっとも駆け引きしてやがらないんだもの」
findings.explanation: Mari is overwhelmingly disadvantaged because she is not playing any romantic game or strategy at all—she has exposed herself completely. The English says she is impossible to persuade, replacing the reason for her vulnerability with stubborn resistance.
findings.japanese:
「特にあいつは、今の段階で圧倒的に不利だからね。
…ちっとも駆け引きしてやがらないんだもの」
findings.todokanai: "Especially considering how severely disadvantaged she is right now. …It's just impossible to persuade her."

findings.highlight: It's a matter of who I could tell that I loved them…
findings.evidenceJa: 「誰に対しても好きって言えないんじゃなくて、誰に対しても好きって言ってしまっただけなんです…」
findings.explanation: Haruki's self-indictment is not that he cannot tell anyone he loves them, but that he has ended up saying it to everyone. The English reduces this to an opaque question of whom he could tell, deleting the serial confession that explains why even a sincere 'I love her' cannot exonerate him.
findings.japanese:
「誰に対しても好きって言えないんじゃなくて、
誰に対しても好きって言ってしまっただけなんです…」
findings.todokanai: "This isn't about me being unable to tell someone I love them. It's a matter of who I could tell that I loved them…"

findings.highlight: even though I'm still in love with Mari-san right now
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺は麻理さんに、昔好きだった人の面影を見てた。麻理さんを、今でも好きな人と同時に好きになった」
findings.explanation: Haruki says he saw in Mari the traces of someone he once loved, and fell for Mari while simultaneously loving a person he still loves now. 今でも好きな人 modifies the other person, not Mari. The English attaches the continuing love to Mari and reverses the temporal/referential structure of his divided heart.
findings.japanese:
「俺は麻理さんに、昔好きだった人の面影を見てた。
麻理さんを、今でも好きな人と同時に好きになった」
findings.todokanai: "I see someone I used to be in love with in Mari-san. And I'm in love with someone else simultaneously, even though I'm still in love with Mari-san right now."

findings.highlight: She's made up her mind not to even look for another man for the next five years!
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつ、この調子じゃ、ものすっごい引きずるよ？５年は新しい男見つけられないの確定よ！」
findings.explanation: Sawako predicts that Mari will certainly be unable to find another man for five years because she will take this breakup so badly. The English says Mari has consciously decided not to look, replacing emotional incapacity with a deliberate plan.
findings.japanese:
「あいつ、この調子じゃ、ものすっごい引きずるよ？
５年は新しい男見つけられないの確定よ！」
findings.todokanai: "Do you have any idea how long this'll keep dragging her down if she keeps this up? She's made up her mind not to even look for another man for the next five years!"

findings.highlight: you can't let her give up on falling in love for the rest of her life!
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうするしかないの！すぐ次の恋に走らせるか、一生恋を諦めさせるかしないと駄目なの！」
findings.explanation: Sawako says Haruki must force a decisive outcome: either send Mari running into a new love immediately or make her give up love for life. The English changes the second explicit alternative into something he must not allow, reversing one branch of the either/or construction.
findings.japanese:
「そうするしかないの！
すぐ次の恋に走らせるか、
一生恋を諦めさせるかしないと駄目なの！」
findings.todokanai: "Well, that's the only way you can do it! You need to push her toward her next love; you can't let her give up on falling in love for the rest of her life!"

findings.highlight: I wouldn't have expected the opportunity to work overseas if I didn't have the confidence.
findings.evidenceJa: 「自信がなきゃ海外赴任なんて希望しないわよ。３０前にせめてデスクにはなっておかないとね」
findings.explanation: Mari says she would not have requested an overseas posting without confidence; the transfer was her active longstanding ambition. The English says she would not have expected the opportunity, making her a passive recipient rather than the person who pursued it.
findings.japanese:
「自信がなきゃ海外赴任なんて希望しないわよ。
３０前にせめてデスクにはなっておかないとね」
findings.todokanai: "I wouldn't have expected the opportunity to work overseas if I didn't have the confidence. I want to at least be promoted to managing editor before I turn 30."

findings.highlight: I guess it's possible that that's the sort of relationship we had…
findings.evidenceJa: 「………冷静に考えてみると、私って、あっち関係では本当にそうかもしれない」
findings.explanation: After Sawako asks whether she is an M, Mari admits that when she thinks calmly, she really may be masochistic in sexual matters. The English says only that theirs may have been that sort of relationship, shifting the discovery from Mari's sexuality to a vague relationship dynamic.
findings.japanese:
「………冷静に考えてみると、
私って、あっち関係では本当にそうかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "…If I calm down and think about it, I guess it's possible that that's the sort of relationship we had…"
